text:
marie_cs: Quick heads up — NewLeaf Bio (trial) emailed asking for a LatAm peering + temporary QPS bump for an Apr 1 pilot. Need allowlist + header pin. Can we triage?

devon_support: Got it. Do we have CIDRs + exact QPS they expect? Also any legal/consent doc required?

marie_cs: Copying details from the customer thread:
- Org: NewLeaf Bio (contact: Alex <alex@newleaf.bio>)
- Window: 2026-04-01 00:00 -> 2026-04-07 23:59 (inclusive)
- Peak expected QPS: ~180 but want burst to 600 for demo -> asking for 600 QPS soft limit
- IPs: 34.210.0.0/16 and 2001:0db8::/32 (they supplied both v4 and v6 ranges)
- Header pin: X-Org-ID: newleaf-bio
- Preferred region: sa-east1 (Brazil) — they want traffic routed to nearest edge

santiago_netops: We can do an allowlist + header inspection at the edge. Need a peering request for sa-east1 and a short maintenance window for config push. Also, which backend pool do they hit? Hosted API or Dedicated?

marie_cs: Hosted API for now. Might move to Dedicated later.

aj_eng_infra: Flagging potential risk: sudden 600 QPS bursts from a trial org could spike per-zone token usage. Suggest temporary soft quota with auto-revoke on anomaly, and KV-prefix caching to avoid repeated context costs. I can add a feature-flagged route for them so we can revert quickly.

carla_pm: Note — renewal discussion scheduled for May. This pilot looks like a conversion opportunity but also a renewal risk if performance issues show up. Capture feedback during the window and include an eval prompt set.

devon_support: I'll draft the customer-facing acceptance email + data handling consent. @aj_eng_infra can you confirm the config is reversible and we can throttle mid-window if needed? :thumbsup:

aj_eng_infra: Yes — we'll gate with feature flag ff:newleaf-bio-peering and a rate-limit override config. Revert is one CLI toggle. Canary rollout first to 2% of traffic, then 25%, then 100. I'll create the canary plan.

santiago_netops: For the edge config I'll prepare this snippet for the proxy team: ```
allowlist_ips: ["34.210.0.0/16","2001:0db8::/32"]
header_whitelist: ["X-Org-ID"]
region_route: "sa-east1"
rate_limit_override: { "qps": 600, "window": "2026-04-01T00:00Z/2026-04-07T23:59Z" }
```
We need an internal peering ticket (NET-1203) and an Ops calendar entry for Apr 1 turnover.

ops-bot: Internal ticket created: CS-2319 — "NewLeaf Bio LatAm peering + temp QPS bump". Owners: devon_support, aj_eng_infra, santiago_netops.

devon_support: I'll attach the customer-signed consent and confirm the CIDRs. Also adding a short SLA note: demo traffic not covered by standard SLA; will confirm in email.

marie_cs: Owner assignments: devon (customer comms + consent), aj (infra rollout + feature flag), santiago (edge config + peering), carla (renewal/feedback capture). I'll update CS-2319 with timelines.

aj_eng_infra: Plan timeline:
- Today: validate CIDRs and legal ok
- T+1 business day: create canary routing and rate override (2% traffic)
- T+2: 25% canary, monitor latency/cost/regressions
- Apr 1: switch to full window if green.

carla_pm: I'll prepare a short eval suite (latency, token-cost per prompt, correctness of X-Org-ID routing) and run daily checks during the window. Add any customer feedback threads to CS-2319.

devon_support: One more ask from Alex — they want the allowlist to include a short-lived header HMAC for additional auth. Is that something we can do without a Private deployment?

aj_eng_infra: We can validate header values at the edge (simple header equality + HMAC check) as long as they provide the key and rotate it. Not ideal for long-term security, but fine for demo with consent. Will need their key and rotation schedule.

marie_cs: Great. I'll collect the key rotation plan and signed consent, and post to CS-2319. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

santiago_netops: Adding note — after window ends, we'll auto-remove allowlist and revert qps override. Please ensure we have a post-mortem checklist to capture any egress peering fees.

devon_support: ACK — will set calendar reminders for Apr 8 to trigger auto-revoke and to collect billing/usage summary.

marie_cs: Closing loop — once the canary is green, we'll share instructions with the customer and get the manual go/no-go from Alex.
